# Full support-cone second-order conditions and an unbounded neutral-index example

This note retains the active compatibility cone and every fixed cap Hessian in a simultaneous physical variation of planar fibers. It gives an exact finite second-order alternative, including changes of cap combinatorics. It then proves that actual criticality, a balanced full-rank circuit, strict compatibility, strict no-heavy volumes, and actual global fixed-cap volume maximality do not alone bound the positive index of the raw volume Hessian by parity. The counterexample has cap fraction 1/2, above OC; it does not refute an additional assertion conditioned on a strict OC violation.

## 1. Planar support coordinates and exact quadratic chambers

Fix a finite lattice-convex integer base P and fixed complete planar normal fans for its positive polygonal fibers. Use the support-array coordinates and linearity subspace of `candidate 94a1565e143d393e`. The actual compatible arrays form a finite polyhedral cone

    A h >= 0.                                                   (1)

All statements below are relative to that coordinate subspace. Work in a bounded neighborhood of an array h* whose fibers have positive area. Positivity persists after small perturbations.

Total mixed area is one quadratic polynomial M(h) on this support cone. One proof uses the oriented boundary formula: every polygon vertex is the intersection of its two incident fixed support lines, hence is linear in h, and shoelace area is quadratic. A common refinement can insert zero-length edges without changing this formula. Equivalently each edge length is linear in h and area is one half the sum of support offset times edge length.

Fix finitely many actual ambient caps H_j. On a fiber at z their continuous inequalities have fixed normal and fixed offset. Add each cap boundary to the fiber's fixed lines. Each candidate intersection of two nonparallel lines is affine in h; its satisfaction of every other line is an affine inequality in h. There are finitely many such candidates. Subdividing the neighborhood by their feasibility inequalities gives finitely many closed polyhedral cells. On each cell, each truncated polygon has a fixed boundary sequence, allowing repeated vertices and zero-length edges on the cell boundary. Its area is therefore an exact quadratic polynomial C_(j,sigma)(h).

This subdivision includes full, empty, supporting-edge and vertex-contact statuses. On common cell faces the formulas have the same values, because they describe the same actual cap volume. Their derivatives need not agree at a supporting edge. No differentiability across such a face is assumed.

Intersect the cells with (1). Write a resulting cell as

    B_sigma h >= c_sigma.                                     (2)

It contains only actual compatible arrays. This description includes all active support convexity, mixed-fiber compatibility, and cap-pattern inequalities; it is not an independent per-fiber relaxation.

## 2. The exact acceleration test at a constrained maximizer

Suppose h* is an actual local maximizer of M among compatible arrays satisfying all fixed cap budgets C_j(h)<=b_j. Let J be the active budgets at h*. Choose any cell sigma containing h*, and let I be the rows of (2) active there. Denote derivatives of its exact quadratic polynomials by

    m=DM(h*),         c_j=DC_(j,sigma)(h*),
    q0(v)=D²M[v,v],   q_j(v)=D²C_(j,sigma)[v,v].

Consider any first velocity v satisfying

    B_I v>=0,     c_j v<=0 for j in J,     m v=0.               (3)

Put

    I(v)={i in I:B_i v=0},
    J(v)={j in J:c_j v=0}.

Then there is NO acceleration w satisfying simultaneously

    B_(I(v)) w>=0,
    c_j w+q_j(v)<0 for every j in J(v),
    m w+q0(v)>0.                                              (4)

Proof. The actual support path h(t)=h*+t v+(t²/2)w stays in (2) for every sufficiently small positive t. An active row with positive first derivative stays positive, and a tied row has nonnegative second coefficient. Inactive rows stay positive by continuity. Thus the path consists of actual compatible positive-area fibers in the same allowed normal-fan class.

Exact quadratic expansion gives

    C_j(h(t))=C_j(h*)+t c_j v
                 +(t²/2)[c_j w+q_j(v)]+O(t³),
    M(h(t))=M(h*)+(t²/2)[m w+q0(v)]+O(t³).

An active cap with a strictly negative first coefficient stays feasible. Every tied active cap strictly decreases by (4); inactive budgets retain their slack. The objective strictly increases. This contradicts actual maximality. The argument is one simultaneous body variation satisfying ALL original budgets. QED.

## 3. The complete multiplier alternative, with its quantifiers

For every velocity in (3), there exist nonnegative theta, lambda_j for j in J(v), and eta_i for i in I(v), such that

    theta+sum_j lambda_j>0,
    theta m = sum_j lambda_j c_j - eta^T B_(I(v)),              (5)
    theta q0(v)-sum_j lambda_j q_j(v)<=0.                     (6)

Here the multipliers may depend on both the first velocity and the chosen cell. In particular, (6) is NOT asserted for every first-order stress.

For completeness, let W={w:B_(I(v))w>=0}. The affine image of W under

    w -> (m w+q0(v), (-c_j w-q_j(v))_(j in J(v)))

does not meet the open positive orthant by Section 2. It is a polyhedron, hence separation gives a nonzero nonnegative normal (theta,lambda) whose inner product with that image is always nonpositive. Because W is a cone containing zero, the constant part is nonpositive and the linear part is nonpositive on W. The polar-cone form of finite-dimensional Farkas gives

    theta m-sum_j lambda_j c_j = -eta^T B_(I(v)), eta>=0,

which proves (5)–(6).

If there is an e with

    B_(I(v))e>=0 and c_j e<0 for every j in J(v),              (7)

then theta>0. Otherwise theta=0 would make lambda nonzero, while evaluating (5) at e gives a strictly negative sum equal to a nonnegative sum, impossible. We may then normalize theta=1. The full necessary Lagrangian condition is

    [D²M-sum_j lambda_j D²C_(j,sigma)][v,v]<=0,               (8)

with the active cone stress in (5) retained. The cone has zero Hessian because its constraints are linear; it still restricts both the velocity and admissible accelerations.

In an open smooth cap-pattern chamber, common erosion from `candidate 21a9da879344205f` supplies (7): it lies in the actual support tangent cone and strictly decreases each positive active cap. This gives a normalized second-order stress for each critical velocity. At a cap-pattern boundary, erosion need not lie in a specified chosen cell. One must either verify (7) in that cell or retain theta>=0 and the other cells. The globally normalized first-order stress alone does not justify discarding this qualification.

This is a finite exact test, stronger in scope than the archived free-simplex physical calculation because all active compatibility rows and all cap-pattern branches are present. It is not a new general nonlinear-programming principle, and it does not itself impose a parity bound.

## 4. An actual strict-noheavy family with arbitrarily large neutral positive index

Take n=1,d=2, any integer m>=2, P={-m,...,m}, and

    r_j=1-j²/(4m²),
    K_j=r_j[-1,1]².                                           (9)

Let r(z) be the piecewise affine interpolation of these values on [-m,m], and set

    C={(z,x,y):-m<=z<=m, |x|<=r(z), |y|<=r(z)}.

The sequence r_j is strictly concave: its second differences are -1/(2m²). Thus r(z) is positive concave, C is a full-dimensional compact convex polytope, and its COMPLETE integer fibers are exactly (9).

The four fixed square support arrays are all r_j. Every nontrivial compatibility inequality is strict: a strictly concave interpolated sequence gives strict Jensen inequality at an integer barycenter whenever at least two distinct integer bases have positive weights. There are finitely many vertex barycentric inequalities. Positivity of all square side lengths is also strict. Consequently an open neighborhood in the product of the fixed four-normal support coordinates is an actual compatible family. This is genuine simultaneous-body freedom, not a formal independent-fiber substitution.

Write V_j=4r_j² and M=sum V_j. Since 3/4<=r_j<=1,

    max_j V_j=4 < (9/8)(2m+1) <= M/2.                       (10)

Every original fiber is strictly nonheavy.

Use the six fixed nonvertical cylindrical caps

    H_(i,+)={u_i.(x,y)>=0}, H_(i,-)={-u_i.(x,y)>=0},
    u_1=(1,2), u_2=(-2,1), u_3=(1,-3).                     (11)

The three positive normals sum to zero and span R², so they form a full-rank positive circuit and their caps cover every continuous fiber space. Their negatives do too. No line in (11) passes through a vertex of any square in (9), because its two coefficients have unequal absolute values. Every restriction is a proper cut, and all cap functions have a fixed smooth quadratic pattern near the original array.

Each K_j is centrally symmetric, so all six cap masses equal

    Q=M/2.                                                   (12)

These caps are genuine globally depth-critical caps at the actual point Y=(0,0,0). Indeed S is centrally symmetric about Y. Every nonvertical through-Y halfspace has mass M/2 because its boundary has zero area in every fiber. A vertical through-Y halfspace has mass (M+V_0)/2. Thus D(Y)=M/2. At any other point, a pair of opposing nonvertical through-point halfspaces has masses summing to M, so its depth is at most M/2. Hence Q is the actual global maximum raw depth.

Impose the six fixed budgets C_(i,sign)<=Q on ALL actual compatible families with base P, allowing arbitrary new shapes. Every competitor satisfies

    M'=C_(1,+)+C_(1,-)<=2Q=M,

because the common boundary is null in each planar fiber. Therefore the original C is an actual GLOBAL fixed-cap volume maximizer. Its maximality is not merely stationary, infinitesimal, or restricted to centered squares.

Now vary the radii physically as r_j(t)=r_j+t a_j. Every sufficiently small signed t preserves strict compatibility and positive radii. Since all six cuts still bisect every fiber,

    M(t)=4 sum_j(r_j+t a_j)²,
    C_(i,sign)(t)=M(t)/2.                                  (13)

The space

    E={a:sum_j r_j a_j=0}                                  (14)

has dimension |P|-1=2m. On E all cap first derivatives and the total-volume first derivative vanish, while

    M''(0)=8 sum_j a_j²>0 for a!=0.                        (15)

Thus the cap-neutral actual tangent space contains a positive-definite subspace of dimension 2m, arbitrarily greater than 2^n=2. All active compatibility constraints have already been retained; none restricts this space at the displayed array. The full-rank balanced circuit has also been retained.

There is no contradiction to constrained second-order maximality. The two opposite cap functions satisfy the exact identity M=C_(1,+)+C_(1,-) on every nearby support array. The normal stress with multipliers one on that pair and zero on the other four has identically zero Lagrangian, including its Hessian. Any acceleration making both cap second derivatives nonpositive necessarily makes the objective second derivative nonpositive. The raw positive volume form in (15) is exactly canceled by cap curvature.

## 5. Scope of the obstruction and remaining below-target issue

The counterexample verifies all of the following simultaneously: actual convex compatibility, planar fixed normal fans, interior support-cone freedom, positive proper traces, a full-rank balanced critical circuit, strict no-heavy volumes, all-direction global-depth certification, and actual global fixed-budget volume maximality. It disproves an unconditional claim that these facts bound the positive index of the raw mixed-area Hessian on cap-neutral velocities by parity or Helly cardinality.

Its cap ratio is Q/M=1/2, whereas the n=1,d=2 OC target is 2/9. It therefore does NOT refute a theorem conditioned on Q/M<2/9. Such a theorem must use that quantitative assumption through additional geometry or through the full cap Hessians; it cannot follow merely from generic constrained maximality, balanced normals, and the number of integer parity classes.

The necessary second-order conditions in Sections 2–3 remain valid for an attained hypothetical below-target fixed-cap maximizer in the bounded-facet construction. No proved inequality here converts that numerical assumption into a positive feasible Lagrangian mode. Replacing the retained cap Hessians by the raw mixed-area form, or imposing a single stress simultaneously for every critical velocity, would reintroduce precisely the invalid shortcuts excluded by this note.
